summary: Incoming fan-in is unbounded in the derived-parallels export: top_k/per_work_cap bound only a chunk's own panel, so removing the score floor let one chunk be everyone's partner (1,178-degree hubs)

analysis.author: Hermes Agent
analysis.content:
MEASURED 2026-08-15 against the v55 score cache (38,459 pairs, fully warm; CPU-only, guru/rerank.py forces CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""). Every number below is a real re-derive, not a simulation.

THE DEFECT. build_panels() bounds a chunk's OUTGOING panel (top_k gather, per_work_cap thin). Nothing bounds its INCOMING fan-in -- how many OTHER chunks' panels list it as a partner. Removing the min_grade floor (todo:ac63de1a, merged in PR #70) removed the only thing accidentally suppressing that. Uncapped v55: 50,148 edges over 5,054 chunks, median degree 10, p99 315, max 1,178 (christian_mysticism.life-and-doctrines-boehme.016; second at 1,159, plato-phaedrus.018).

guru-web's LIMIT 100 read-time query (todo:bc084b37) bounds what a READER sees, not what ships in edges_derived.jsonl, so any other consumer of the export gets the unbounded tail.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG. A degree budget charged to BOTH endpoints -- skip the edge when either is full -- reads as equivalent and is not: it lets a chunk's own accumulated degree veto its neighbours' edges. Replayed at 100: 50,148 -> 21,008 edges; only 129 chunks were ever over cap, but 4,531 UNDER-cap chunks lost edges and 367 ended with zero partners. That hands back a large share of the coverage the floor removal had just won (the floor removal's whole result was chunks-with-panels 2,364 -> 5,054).

Charging only the RECEIVING leg fixes the mechanism: an edge dies only when the chunk it points AT is over its own budget. Mutual pairs (both endpoints picked each other) are outgoing for both, so they are kept and charged to neither.

BUT THE MECHANISM WAS NOT THE MAIN PROBLEM -- THE THRESHOLD WAS. Correct fan-in at 100 gives 21,476 edges / 353 darkened, against the both-endpoints version's 21,008 / 367. A 468-edge difference. The cause is the degree distribution: 41,807 of 50,148 edges (83%) touch one of the 129 chunks above 100, so 129 hubs x 100 slots = 12,900 slots for 41,807 hub-bound edges. At that threshold ANY fan-in cap must delete most of the graph. That is arithmetic, not implementation.

SWEEP (true fan-in, edges kept / chunks left with NO partners, against 50,148 / 5,054 uncapped):
  1000 -> 49,830 / 0    500 -> 44,330 / 0    200 -> 31,120 / 48
   750 -> 48,168 / 0    400 -> 41,613 / 0    150 -> 26,769 / 134
                        300 -> 37,713 / 3    100 -> 21,476 / 353
Chunk darkening -- a chunk dropping out of the graph entirely -- is the hard failure and starts below 400. Uncapped p99 degree is 315, so 500 bites only the genuine outliers (max degree 1,178 -> 516) while keeping 88% of edges. 100 is not a tail trim; it is a second score floor wearing a degree cap's clothes.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE. A cap that (a) charges only the receiving leg, (b) is set from the measured sweep rather than a round number, (c) reports its own blast radius in summary.json so the node-16 eyeball gate can catch a run that halves the graph, and (d) leaves zero chunks darkened.

SHIPPING IS NOT PART OF THIS TICKET. The cap changes exported edge counts (50,148 -> 44,330 at 500), so it needs a re-export and the owner's deploy gate. Cutover verification is tracked at todo:9097deed. Stop at the artifact.

PROVENANCE NOTE. export.py's _find_latest_run_dir() takes the lexicographically latest subdirectory of data/derived_parallels/ with no provenance check, so any experimental run written there silently becomes the next export's source -- including a --limit-concepts smoke run. Write experiments elsewhere.
